cron_timing_note: Cron runs in UTC. One-shot crons scheduled 5-8 minutes ahead on specific minutes, read once via the cron-jobs output operation, then deleted immediately — none left armed (verified empty via a cron-jobs list call after smoke-test-live). One migrate-apply create-cron call in this deploy failed client-side with a transient DNS error (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND developers.hostinger.com) before reaching Hostinger at all; a cron-jobs list call confirmed no job had actually been created, so the retry was safe and did not double-schedule anything — worth that same list-to-confirm check any time a cron-create call itself errors, rather than assuming it's safe (or unsafe) to retry blind. 2026-10-03 addendum: a one-time cron whose minute has already passed never fires and its output stays empty forever (it happened twice, because the gap between reading the clock and creating the cron was many minutes). Schedule >=10-12 minutes ahead, create the cron immediately after reading the clock, and confirm by an ls/file-API probe instead of assuming. A `* * * * *` job running a harmless command is a fast way to read server state; delete it after. `%` in a cron command is eaten by crontab. TUS upload credentials stop working (403) well before their 6 h expiry.

The upload step's own generateUploadURLV1 call must target the domain admin.provatferi.org (the subdomain itself), not the parent provatferi.org — the parent domain's upload URL roots at that domain's own public_html (wrong tree entirely for this subdomain's docroot), while the subdomain's own upload URL roots directly at its docroot, matching upload-release.mjs's un-prefixed `_release_staging/...` destination path exactly.

curl_csrf_testing_note: When scripting a POST to a CSRF-protected route (e.g. /locale) with curl, fetch the CSRF token and set the cookie jar in the SAME request that will be reused for the POST, not across separate GET calls with the jar re-opened each time — doing it in two disjoint GET calls produced a spurious 419 in an earlier session even though the actual endpoint was working correctly.
monorepo_note: admin-erp/ and institutional/ are two subdirectories of ONE git repository (same origin remote, same commit history) — a commit that only touches one of the two still shares a SHA history with the other. build-release.sh already handles this correctly (it has throughout this engagement): it archives and ships only the admin-erp/ subtree for this pipeline. upload_race_fix_2026_10_05.summary: The stage->switch upload race is fixed. Before: `stage` copied the live uploads tree once (count-checked); uploads the live app accepted until `switch` went to the OLD tree, which the switch renamed to _previous-<ts> carrying nothing over (rows kept, files lost). Now: stage records a hash manifest; switch runs a three-way merge (snapshot / live / staged) until convergence BEFORE the rename, the two renames recover from a stray application directory, and additive post-rename sweeps (immediately, after 10 s, and in smoke-test-live) prove nothing is left only in the retired tree. Collisions are never overwritten (switch refuses before renaming; `keep-both` preserves the other copy under _upload-conflicts/). reconcile <retired> recovers files an older release stranded. See deploy/README.md 'Uploads during a deploy'.
upload_race_fix_2026_10_05.reproduced: ReleaseSwitchUploadsTest ran the REAL release-manager.php stage->switch in a sandbox copy of the production layout against the unmodified code: scenario B failed with 'THE RACE: a CV uploaded after stage was left behind in the retired tree' (also: a file replaced after stage came out stale; a write into the retired tree after the rename was never carried).
upload_race_fix_2026_10_05.tests: tests/Feature/Deploy: 80 passed, 3 skipped (symlink/POSIX-mode cases cannot run on the Windows dev host) — 43 new tests (ReleaseSwitchUploadsTest A-F + deletes + legacy manifest + double switch + install, ReleaseSwitchUploadsEdgeCasesTest rollback/reconcile/sweeps/never-stopping writer/stray dir, UploadsSyncTest library). Whole ERP suite in build-release.sh: 642 passed, 3 skipped. Seven mutations (overwrite on collision, no sweeps, no stray handling, no delete propagation, sweep resurrects, no staged-app guard, install forgets the lib) are each caught by at least one test; the never-stopping-writer test fails without the post-rename sweep.
